subject: Post-demo compliance recap: subprocessors, retention windows, and SOC 2 timeline
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo compliance recap: subprocessors, retention windows, and SOC 2 timeline

Hi Lisa / BrightHealth team — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and asks so we can keep procurement moving:  

1) SOC 2 / audit evidence: you mentioned an upcoming SOC 2 Type II renewal in Q3. Can you confirm the expected delivery month for the report and whether we can share a redacted copy with procurement under NDA? We will need the period covered for our security review.

2) Data scope & retention: BrightHealth flagged that PHI may be in-scope for some flows. Please confirm the retention windows you expect Redwood to support for session logs, full audit logs, and PII/PHI extracted from transcripts. Typical options we've seen: 30/90/365 days or customer-configurable retention — please advise.

3) Subprocessors / cloud providers: to complete BrightHealth's vendor inventory, please confirm which cloud providers and managed services at a minimum will touch BrightHealth data when using Redwood Hosted and Redwood Dedicated. In particular: GCP (region), AWS (region), any Azure components, CDN/edge caches, and our optional third-party analytics tooling.

4) Security questionnaire / next steps: if you can share the Security team contact or the questionnaire link, we'll prioritize returning the completed matrix this week. We attached our latest subprocessor matrix and a simplified data-flow diagram for reference.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v1.xlsx], [Attachment: data_flow_diagram_v2.png]  

Proposed next steps: short call with your security lead + our compliance eng (Marissa) for 30 minutes this week to walk the matrix and outstanding items. Suggested times: Wed 7/14 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 7/15 08:00–09:00 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks — Naomi

Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo compliance recap: subprocessors, retention windows, and SOC 2 timeline

Hi Naomi — great meeting, thanks. A few quick answers:  

• SOC 2: we completed a Type II in Jan 2026; our annual assessment is scheduled for late Aug 2027. We can share a redacted Jan 2026 report today under NDA; procurement prefers a redacted PDF.

• PHI & retention: for our use-case PHI is limited to clinician notes in transcripts. Procurement's baseline requirement is 365 days for application-level logs and 7 years for records tied directly to patient treatment (we understand that may be handled via integration / long-term storage on their side). We need to confirm whether Redwood's hosted logs can be set to 7-year archival exports for customers on Dedicated or Private.

• Subprocessors: security@brighthealth.com will need your canonical subprocessor list. For starters we expect you to supply exact cloud regions and any third-party telemetry/analytics endpoints.

Link to our security intake form: https://brighthealth.atlassian.net/secure/attach/SEC-forms/Redwood-intake

I'll loop Tom Rivers (our third-party security consultant) to help triage details and coordinate with procurement. Wed 7/14 10:00 PT works for a 30-minute sync for me.

—Lisa
Lisa Chen
Sr. Manager, Vendor Risk | BrightHealth
lisa.chen@brighthealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo compliance recap: subprocessors, retention windows, and SOC 2 timeline

Forwarding our internal subprocessor matrix and a short note on capability gaps. Attached: redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v1.xlsx, SOC2-type2-summary.pdf, data_flow_diagram_v2.png.  

Marissa here (Security & Compliance @ Redwood) — quick clarifications to set expectations before the call:  

• Hosted (Redwood API): primary compute runs on GCP us-central1 and us-west2 for low-latency routing; customer data may traverse AWS us-east-1 for async batch jobs in specific regions (we document per-customer routing in the contract). We use FastCache (edge CDN) for streaming optimization — it only caches encrypted token-level pointers, not decrypted content.

• Dedicated / Private: Dedicated pools can be provisioned in AWS or GCP regions of choice; Private (VPC) deployments can be air-gapped per procurement requirements and support customer-managed KMS/HSM for key control.

• Retention controls: we offer configurable retention windows at the customer level for session data (30/90/365 days). For customers requiring archival beyond 365 days we provide export hooks to long-term storage (S3/GCS) or can work with procurement for dedicated archival pipelines.

• Audit evidence: SOC 2 Type II summary attached. Full report can be shared under NDA; we can provide auditor contact if needed.

Action items I am taking before Wed's call: attach canonical subprocessor CSV exported from the matrix, add region-by-region routing notes, and include a short appendix describing encryption-in-transit and KMS options.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick follow-ups ahead of the call:  

1) Can Redwood confirm the retention and purging workflow for PHI on Hosted plans? Specifically: where is the canonical copy stored, what job/process purges it, and can deletion be audited?

2) Please confirm the default encryption-at-rest algorithm and whether customer-managed KMS is available on Dedicated/Private (we need KMS key rotation logs for our audit).

3) Log access and identity: who in Redwood has access to raw transcripts and audit logs (roles + justification)? We need a brief RBAC breakdown to present to our compliance committee.

If you can drop the short RBAC list and a one-paragraph description of the purge workflow to the Drive link Lisa shared, that will speed procurement. Also happy to take 15 mins pre-call to save time.

—Tom
